name: Containerised Application
description: A pattern for deploying applications as container images orchestrated by a managed container platform. Provides consistent deployment artefacts, environment parity, and horizontal scaling while abstracting away underlying infrastructure management.
whenToUse: Applications requiring consistent deployment across development, staging, and production
Microservices architectures where each service has independent scaling requirements
Teams with container expertise wanting portable deployments across cloud providers
Workloads requiring fine-grained resource allocation and horizontal auto-scaling
Applications with complex dependency stacks that benefit from containerised isolation
whenNotToUse: Simple applications where serverless would provide lower operational overhead
Teams without container or Kubernetes expertise and no capacity to learn
Workloads with very low traffic where container orchestration overhead is unjustified
Legacy applications that cannot be containerised without significant refactoring
Scenarios where the organisation lacks CI/CD maturity for container image pipelines

typicalComponents.name: Container Orchestrator
typicalComponents.purpose: Schedule, scale, and manage container lifecycle across a cluster
typicalComponents.technology: Amazon ECS, Azure Container Apps, or Google Kubernetes Engine

typicalComponents.name: Container Registry
typicalComponents.purpose: Store and distribute container images with vulnerability scanning
typicalComponents.technology: Amazon ECR, Azure Container Registry, or Artifact Registry

typicalComponents.name: Service Mesh
typicalComponents.purpose: Manage service-to-service communication, observability, and security
typicalComponents.technology: AWS App Mesh, Istio, or Linkerd

typicalComponents.name: Ingress Controller
typicalComponents.purpose: Route external traffic to appropriate container services
typicalComponents.technology: ALB Ingress, Azure Application Gateway, or GKE Ingress

typicalComponents.name: CI/CD Pipeline
typicalComponents.purpose: Build container images, scan for vulnerabilities, and deploy to clusters
typicalComponents.technology: GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps, or Cloud Build

securityControls: Scan container images for vulnerabilities in the CI/CD pipeline before deployment
Use minimal base images and run containers as non-root users
Implement network policies to restrict pod-to-pod communication
Sign container images and enforce signature verification at deployment
Implement secrets management using platform-native secret stores
Apply pod security standards to prevent privilege escalation
Regularly update base images and rebuild containers to patch vulnerabilities
resilienceConsiderations: Container orchestrators automatically restart failed containers and reschedule across nodes
Horizontal pod autoscaling responds to traffic increases automatically
Deploy across multiple availability zones for infrastructure resilience
Implement health checks (liveness and readiness probes) for automatic recovery
Use rolling deployments to achieve zero-downtime releases
Implement pod disruption budgets to maintain availability during cluster maintenance
costConsiderations: Compute costs based on cluster capacity — right-size nodes and use spot/preemptible instances
Container orchestration management fees (ECS is free, EKS/GKE have control plane costs)
Container registry storage and data transfer costs
Operational costs for team training and Kubernetes expertise
Consider Fargate/serverless containers to avoid cluster management overhead
Implement resource requests and limits to prevent over-provisioning
operationalConsiderations: Team must have container and orchestration expertise or invest in training
Cluster upgrades and node patching require planned maintenance procedures
Monitoring must cover cluster health, pod metrics, and application-level observability
Log aggregation needed across multiple container instances
Capacity planning for cluster node pools and auto-scaling limits
Incident response procedures for container-specific failure modes

services.name: Amazon ECS with Fargate
services.purpose: Serverless container orchestration without cluster management

services.name: Amazon ECR
services.purpose: Container image registry with vulnerability scanning

questionsToAsk: Does the team have existing container and Kubernetes expertise?
Is full Kubernetes needed or would a simpler container service (ECS, Container Apps) suffice?
What is the expected scaling profile — steady state or highly variable?
Are there compliance requirements around container image provenance and signing?
What CI/CD tooling is already in place for building and deploying containers?
Is multi-cloud portability a genuine requirement or a theoretical concern?
commonMistakes: Adopting Kubernetes when a simpler container service would meet requirements with less overhead
Running containers as root or using bloated base images with unnecessary packages
Not implementing resource limits, allowing a single container to consume all cluster resources
Treating containers as VMs — running multiple processes per container instead of one
Not scanning container images for vulnerabilities before deployment to production
